# `aitbc gpu-onchain deregister`

Deactivate an on-chain GPU registration (signed by its registrant). The registration stays on the chain with status 'deactivated' and takes no new allocations; registering the same gpu-id again reactivates it. Takes effect only once the chain has activated state-transition v10; before that the node refuses the transaction. This is not `aitbc gpu unregister`, which only edits the local GPU service.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc gpu-onchain deregister [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--gpu-id` | text | — | yes | GPU ID to take out of service |
| `--wallet` | text | — | yes | Wallet name for signing (must be the GPU's registrant) |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |
| `--wait` | flag | `false` | no | Wait for the transaction to be mined |
| `--format` | choice | — | no | Output format |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc gpu-onchain deregister --gpu-id <gpu_id> --wallet <wallet>
```
